rationale: Both reviews are deeply evidence-grounded and share several valid findings (T2VA accuracy-gate removal, unpinned MODEL_REVISION, media_utils.py's shared blast radius, ref2va audio truncation risk), so precision is comparably high. Y has notably better recall of the ground-truth inline concerns: it explicitly credits the workdir-removal fix (matching the resolved 'workdir dead arg' nit) and flags that the new sampling test can't catch a frame-count-source mismatch (echoing the 'weak test' concern), plus it names the red CI gates explicitly; X only tangentially brushes the rank-order/hang concern via a test-robustness note and never mentions workdir or the weak-sampling-test issue at all. Y also surfaces more substantive, well-reasoned issues beyond the ground truth (lossless-RGB memory/disk lifecycle, double-decode frame-count mismatch, nightly time budget, CDN asset fragility, snapshot_download post-condition, offload-staging inconsistency) with concrete fixes, giving it an actionability edge.
